source.title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions

accepted.question_text: What is the physical nature of the S11(1535) resonance that dominates eta-meson production from single nucleons: is it a compact quark-model baryon state, a dynamically generated state, or specifically an eta-nucleon molecular state? A self-contained resolution should explain how the energy dependence of the elastic eta-nucleon scattering amplitude in the eta-nucleon channel can distinguish a molecule from a compact state, despite the fact that direct elastic eta-nucleon scattering is experimentally inaccessible, and should derive useful constraints on the eta-nucleon scattering parameters from available non-diagonal hadronic and photon-induced reactions.
accepted.context_brief: Nature of S11(1535) and eta-nucleon scattering

evidence.quote: It is well known that the production of eta mesons from single nucleons is dominated by the resonance S11(1535) irrespective of the probe.

Especially since the nature of this resonance is heavily debated in the literature (see also next section and references given there), a systematic study of η production in various environments is of high importance.

How is it possible to distinguish molecular states and compact quark states? Based on an old proposal by Weinberg [17] in Ref. [18], in line with a series of older works [19], we identified the energy dependence of the elastic scattering amplitude in the molecule forming channel as a key quantity.
Thus, to understand if the S11 is an ηN molecule, experimental information is needed on elastic ηN scattering. Unfortunately this channel is not directly accessible.

To summarize the investigations based on reactions on a single baryon we state that in order to better understand the nature of the S11(1535) both high accuracy data and theoretical studies are necessary to derive constraints on the ηN scattering parameters.

accepted.question_text: What, if any, is the relationship between the two proposed explanations of the unexpectedly low Roper resonance in the light-baryon spectrum: the picture in which the Roper resonance is dynamically generated and P11(1710) is the first quark state, and the picture in which a flavor-dependent quark-quark interaction changes the ordering of states? A satisfactory answer should also address how the situation changes if chiral dynamics really makes S11(1535) a dynamically generated state, because that would worsen the disagreement between the low-lying baryon spectrum and the original nonrelativistic quark-model ordering.

evidence.quote: To my understanding there are so far two possible explanations of the spectrum in the literature, one, where the Roper is generated dynamically and thus interpreting the P11(1710) as the first quark state [12,13], and another, where the ordering of states was changed by introducing a flavor dependent quark–quark interaction [14].
At present it is not clear what the connection between these two pictures is — if such a connection exits at all.
Recently the whole situation became even more confusing for it was claimed that based on chiral dynamics the S11(1535) appears as a dynamically generated state [15,16].
It is therefore of high importance to understand the nature of the low lying resonances for this promises deep insights into how the nature makes hadrons.

accepted.question_text: How do a loosely bound eta-nucleon molecular interpretation and a compact quark-state interpretation of S11(1535) behave differently when additional baryons are present, and can a systematic theoretical approach be developed for eta-deuteron and eta-helium-3 systems that uses those differences to test the nature of S11(1535)?

evidence.quote: In addition, it is expected that a (loosely bound) molecule and a compact quark state behave very different in the presence of additional baryons.
This field is unfortunately still lacking a systematic approach at present, although microscopic calculations are available for both the ηd [26] and the η3He [27] system.

accepted.question_text: What mechanism explains the failure of models that reproduce the total pp → pp eta cross section to reproduce the pp invariant-mass spectrum near threshold? The alternatives to disentangle are a significant eta-nucleon interaction not captured by the existing model, an energy dependence of the production operator, and significant nucleon-nucleon P-wave contributions; a resolution should use observables such as the double-polarization observable Axx together with differential cross sections to isolate nucleon-nucleon P-waves and establish the partial-wave decomposition of the pp eta spectrum.

evidence.quote: However, it turned out that the pp invariant mass spectrum measured for pp → ppη [3] can not be described in this way — the data is shown in Fig. 4.

To resolve the discrepancy it was speculated that either there is a significant ηN interaction [31], not captured by the model of Ref. [29]. On the contrary, Deloff argued that there might be a significant energy dependence of the production operator [32], and in Ref. [33] a significant contribution of NN P–waves were proposed as a possible solution for the puzzle.
However, such a dependence would emerge from all three explanations. Fortunately it is possible to isolate the NN P–waves by a double polarized measurement.
It should be clear that only when the partial wave decomposition of the ppη spectrum is known, we can understand the role the ηN interaction plays here.

accepted.question_text: How can scattering lengths or other eta-nucleus scattering parameters be quantitatively and reliably extracted from eta-production data when final-state interactions, effective-range corrections, and inelastic channels are present? A solution should go beyond using the Watson-Migdal scattering-length formula only qualitatively, because the direct proportionality between production and elastic scattering energy dependences holds only when the scattering length is much larger than the effective range, and because no closed-form final-state-interaction expression is available in the presence of inelasticities.
accepted.context_brief: Extracting eta-nucleus scattering from production data

evidence.quote: Note that one should be careful in interpreting the value of a extracted from a fit to production data as the scattering length.

However, a direct proportionality between the energy dependence of scattering and production only holds, if the scattering length is significantly larger than the next term in the effective range expansion — the effective range.

One should also stress that in the presence of inelasticities it is not even possible to derive an expression for the final state interaction effect in closed form. Thus the results should be taken on a qualitative level.

accepted.question_text: How can experiments determine the sign of the real part of the eta-nucleus scattering length, rather than only its magnitude, so that a near-threshold eta-nucleus pole can be classified as a bound state or a virtual state? The problem requires high-accuracy measurements of the eta-nucleus amplitude both above threshold, where observables are sensitive to the magnitude of the real part, and below threshold through inelastic channels that couple significantly to the eta-nucleus channel.

evidence.quote: It is the sign of the real part that decides, whether the nearby pole we want to investigate refers to a bound state or a virtual state.

Thus any measurement above the η–nucleus threshold is sensitive only to the magnitude of the real part, but not to its sign; measurements above threshold are necessary to pin down the absolute values of the real and the imaginary part of the scattering length.

Since we know the sign of the imaginary part high accuracy measurements of the energy dependence of the η–nucleus amplitude above and below the eta threshold allows one to extract the sign of the real part of the scattering length [44].
But what does it mean to measure an amplitude below threshold? This can only work by identifying inelastic channels that show a significant coupling to the η–nucleus channel.

accepted.question_text: Why can the imaginary part of the eta-helium-3 scattering length be compatible with zero even though the pi-nucleon to eta-nucleon channel couples significantly near threshold and might suggest an imaginary part of order at least one fermi? The proposed resolution to assess is whether Pauli-principle blocking of the pi-NN intermediate state suppresses the most prominent inelastic channel in eta-deuteron and, to some extent, eta-helium-3 systems.

evidence.quote: One might therefore expect an imaginary part of the scattering length of the order of at least one fermi.
In contrast to this in a recent analysis of the world data base for η3He values for the imaginary part of the η3He scattering length were extracted that were compatible with zero [43].
Can we understand such a small imaginary part of the scattering length? The answer is yes.
As a consequence the potentially most prominent inelastic channel is blocked.
As the deuteron is a prominent building block also of 3He this argument at least to some extend should hold as well.

accepted.question_text: Is the energy dependence of the eta-helium-3 interaction largely governed by the interaction of the eta meson with the deuteron substructure inside helium-3? This question is motivated by the observed similarity between eta-deuteron and eta-helium-3 interaction energy dependences when both are plotted using cross-section-derived final-state-interaction amplitudes.

evidence.quote: When plotted in the same figure both the ηd interaction and the η3He interaction show a very similar energy dependence.
This similarity might point at the conjecture used above, namely that the η3He dynamics is at least to a large extend given by the interaction of the η with the deuteron substructure of the He.

accepted.question_text: Does the eta-helium-3 system realize a near-threshold eta-nucleus bound state or a virtual state? A resolution should determine the sign of the real part of the eta-helium-3 scattering length using sufficiently accurate below-threshold data, such as inelastic-channel measurements or high-statistics gamma helium-3 to pi-zero p X data, because existing analyses of TAPS/MAMI data favored the virtual-state scenario but could not exclude a bound state.
accepted.context_brief: Eta-helium-3 bound state versus virtual state

evidence.quote: However, to make this analysis useful we need to know, if a bound state exists or not.
Since the existing data is not of sufficient accuracy and there is currently no new measurement planed, we will not describe this here in detail.
Thus the data prefers the solution that corresponds to a virtual state, although the existence of a bound state can not be excluded, given the quality of the data.
The expected much higher statistics promise for a near future an unambiguous decision on what scenario is realized: a bound state or a virtual state.

needs_review.question_text_raw: What should be studied in the coming years in respect to η production from hadrons; theory side a lot still needs to be done.

evidence.quote: In this article I will present my personal point of view of what should be studied in the coming years in respect to η production from hadrons.
Especially on the theory side a lot still needs to be done, but this field of research promises deep insight in strong interaction physics in the non–perturbative regime.

trace.notes: Resolved arXiv abs URL to the PDF, downloaded it to the parser temp directory, and mapped the 12-page PDF. Title and section hierarchy were visible in the source text: introductory remarks, production from single nucleons and S11, NN → ηNN, pd → η3He and γ3He → η3He, summary, acknowledgments, and references.
Introductory remarks yielded the debated S11(1535) nature and a broad programmatic statement about future eta-production studies.

The single-nucleon/S11 section yielded candidates on baryon-spectrum model connections, distinguishing molecular and compact states, inaccessible elastic eta-nucleon scattering, the need for eta-nucleon scattering constraints, and behavior with additional baryons.

The NN → eta NN section yielded the pp → pp eta invariant-mass discrepancy and the unresolved alternatives of eta-nucleon interaction, production-operator energy dependence, and nucleon-nucleon P-waves.

The eta-nucleus section yielded candidates on interpreting scattering lengths from production data, determining the sign of the real scattering length, the small imaginary eta-helium-3 scattering length, eta-helium-3 deuteron substructure, and the eta-helium-3 bound-state versus virtual-state question.
The summary reinforced the broad need for theory development but did not add a new self-contained technical question beyond the accepted candidates.

Expanded the compressed S11 nature question with the source-supported criterion based on the eta-nucleon elastic scattering amplitude and the experimental inaccessibility of direct eta-nucleon elastic scattering.
Converted the explicit uncertainty about the connection between two baryon-spectrum pictures into a standalone question and included the S11 dynamically generated complication supported on page 2.

Converted the statement that molecular and compact states should behave differently with additional baryons, while the field lacks a systematic approach, into a self-contained few-baryon-environment question.
Merged the pp invariant-mass-spectrum discrepancy, the three proposed mechanisms, double-polarization isolation of P-waves, and the need for partial-wave decomposition into one question.

Converted methodological caveats about extracting scattering lengths from production data into a question about quantitative final-state-interaction treatment with effective-range and inelastic-channel limitations.
Expanded the sign-of-real-scattering-length issue with the source-supported distinction between above-threshold magnitude sensitivity and below-threshold sign sensitivity.
Preserved the source's explicit question about the small imaginary eta-helium-3 scattering length and marked it solved because the same source answers yes via Pauli-principle blocking.
Converted the deuteron-substructure conjecture into a standalone eta-helium-3 dynamics question.
Expanded the eta-helium-3 bound-state question with the TAPS/MAMI virtual-state preference and the explicit statement that a bound state could not be excluded.
The broad future-work/theory-development language could not be turned into a precise self-contained research question without adding unsupported scope, so it was moved to needs_review.
Merged the S11 nature, eta-nucleon molecule, inaccessible elastic eta-nucleon channel, and eta-nucleon scattering-parameter constraints into one canonical candidate.
Merged near-duplicate pp → pp eta discrepancy candidates concerning eta-nucleon interaction, production-operator energy dependence, P-waves, Axx, and partial-wave decomposition.
Kept the general sign-of-real-scattering-length measurement problem distinct from the specific eta-helium-3 bound-state versus virtual-state problem.
Kept the eta-helium-3 bound-state versus virtual-state question distinct from the general sign-measurement methodology because it relies on specific pd and TAPS/MAMI evidence.
Accepted questions q_001 through q_009 passed self-containedness, evidence coverage, evidence completeness, no-new-facts, source adequacy, solved-status, and schema gates.
Moved to needs_review because the source text is programmatic and too broad to form a precise standalone research question without unsupported narrowing.
